first.rationale: The concurrent decline in onboarding completion and activation makes onboarding friction the most actionable likely bottleneck to sustainable qualified revenue. Simplification previously improved completion, time-to-value, and early adoption; activation messaging is a secondary complementary lever. Promotional pricing is highly consequential given competitive pressure, but its acquisition lift may not translate to durable qualified revenue, so its archived evidence should be verified alongside the onboarding evidence before commitment.

final.rationale: Run a shortened-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and likely contributes to the 6% activation decline. Verified evidence shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%, supporting sustainable qualified-revenue value. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue short term, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and did not survive the first renewal cycle.
